components.input_conditions: The specified unconditioned Gaussian factor; public large L.
components.parameter_and_cost_changes: Public universal scale; no product-cost inflation.
components.preserved_model_properties: H is a real symmetric instance; PSD and well conditioning are asserted only on the spectral event. W is always PSD with a.s. rank d−k.
remaining_obligations: Any changed shift or prior needs new spectral and posterior analysis.
components.transcript_control: The affine oracle conversion is exact and costs one product, preserving the actual transcript information.
components.transformation: Use H=I−W/L and S=2W/L−W²/L². On ||W||_op≤L/2, H has k unit eigenvalues and all other eigenvalues in [1/2,1); 3W/(2L)≤S≤2W/L.

components.input_conditions: Uniform branch k+q≤d/2; bounded-rank case 1≤k<K_*, with thresholds fixed after K_*.
components.parameter_and_cost_changes: Requires d≥d_{K_*},d≥M_{K_*}k,q≤alpha_{K_*}d. Constants become universal after fixing K_*.
components.preserved_model_properties: Keeps the unconditioned instance law and arbitrary measurable output coverage.
components.transcript_control: The conditional fresh-square comparison is integrated before intersecting other events; independence of spectral events is not assumed.
components.transformation: Use simultaneous fresh small eigenvalues and rectangular lower spectrum. For bounded rank, use square/one-extra-row hard-edge CDF gap F_0(3/4)−F_1(4/5)>1/3, then retain an unconditional probability ≥1/3+rho_{K_*} through continuity and union bounds.

components.parameter_and_cost_changes: No extra queries; arbitrary m×n dimensions.
components.preserved_model_properties: Preserves nonzero singular values and optimal tails, and bounds the extracted square residual by the padded residual.
components.transcript_control: One square product simulates each padded directional product.
components.transformation: Use the complete source-local zero-padding argument recorded in the Gaussian baseline family's zero-padding component: restrict the output basis, complete its range to dimension k and use PSD order of squared residuals.

construction.definition: Sample X in R^{d×(d−k)} with iid N(0,1/d) entries; W=XX^T, K=ker W. Set H=I−W/L and S=I−H²=2W/L−W²/L² with public sufficiently large universal L. Sample once without truncating on a spectral event. For rectangular targets embed H as J_m H J_n^T, d≤N=min(m,n). Fixed-p §5 takes L=2C_0 from Lemma 5.2; uniform §6 uses a sufficiently large universal L and thresholds from Lemma 6.1.
construction.hidden_objects: X,W,K and the positive spectral profile. K is Haar distributed on Gr(k,d). The independent algorithm seed is included in the actual transcript, not in the sampled instance.
construction.parameters: Construction: 1≤k<d. Fixed-p hardness: d≥Ck, k,q≤d/100, d≤eta_p k epsilon^(−1/3). Uniform branch: R=min(N,k Phi), R>M_0 k, d=floor(eta R), d≥M_{K_*}k,d≥d_{K_*},d≥d_0,k≤d/4,q≤alpha d,k+q≤d/2; constants chosen in §8 order. Spectral branch replaces R by min(N,k/sqrt(epsilon)).
construction.public_information: d,k,L, distribution and requested LRA parameters; neither realized factor nor hidden nullspace is disclosed. The favourable spectral event is an analysis event, not a conditioned sampling promise.

hardness_claims.algorithm_coverage: All measurable randomized adaptive exact-product algorithms; unrestricted right-projector output.
hardness_claims.missing_lifting: No claim that this family alone proves the entire min-envelope. No noisy/finite-precision or expected-budget extension.
hardness_claims.regime_note: Only the R>M_0 k branch of Theorem 3.1. For large k failure event ≥0.9; for bounded k Lemma 6.4 gives >1/3 after all required intersections. Rank baseline handles R=O(k).

hardness_claims.algorithm_coverage: All measurable randomized adaptive exact-product algorithms with independent seed.
hardness_claims.missing_lifting: Constants may depend on fixed p; this overlap argument alone is not uniform-p hardness.
hardness_claims.regime_note: Fixed finite p: R>M_p k, d=floor(eta_p R), k,q≤d/100; unconditional success ≤0.15 for q≤d/100 at the chosen dimension.

oracle_realizations.choices_and_history: Every measurable randomized fully adaptive policy with independent seed; arbitrary transcript-measurable rank-k output P. The algorithm sees actual products only, not latent Gaussian rotations or enlarged conditioning fields.
oracle_realizations.cost: Each vector product costs one; b-vector blocks cost b; both directional products cost two; computation and storage free.
oracle_realizations.information_bottleneck: For q≤d−k informative queries, Lemma 4.1 leaves D_q in R^{(d−q)×(d−k−q)} independent iid N(0,1/d) conditional on almost every transcript. Theorem 4.6 bounds E tr(P Pi_K)≤2k(q+k)/(d−q). Theorem 6.3 leaves all first h=d−k−q compression eigenvalues at most Cj²/(dh), conditionally with probability ≥0.95; for k+q≤d/2 this is C'j²/d².
oracle_realizations.information_to_error: On the ≥0.95 fixed-p spectral event H has spectrum in [1/2,1], and success forces k−tr(P Pi_K)≤C_p epsilon d³/k², hence overlap ≥3k/4 at the stated scale; posterior overlap makes overall success ≤0.15. Uniformly for p≥2, compare compression theta_j with positive s_j≥c(k+j)²/d² through R_p=sum(1−theta_j)^(p/2), Z_p=sum(1−s_j)^(p/2). Large-rank excess/ratio and bounded-rank strict edge separation are essential; their calibrated statements and proof map are in the linked uniform theorem.
oracle_realizations.query_and_feedback: Query v and obtain Hv. One W product simulates Hv=v−Wv/L; conversely Wv=L(v−Hv). H is symmetric, so transpose access gives no additional information per charged product. Padded products restrict/embed coordinates.
oracle_realizations.sampling_and_reuse: One unconditioned X reused for the full transcript. The fresh Gaussian block in Lemma 4.1 is posterior residual randomness, not newly resampled oracle noise.

use_restrictions: Conditional spectral properties are not unconditional membership promises for every sample.
